Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## To bang or not to bang

Should I call a method `do_something` or `do_something!`?

As a general rule, we only use `!` for methods that have a correspondent counterpart without `!`. In particular, we don’t use `!` to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

module FixturesTestHelper
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    def identify(label, column_type = :integer)
      if label.to_s.end_with?("_uuid")

    def generate_fixture_uuid(label)
      # Generate deterministic UUIDv7 for fixtures that sorts by fixture ID
      # This allows .first/.last to work as expected in tests
      # Use the same CRC32 algorithm as Rails' default fixture ID generation
      # so that UUIDs sort in the same order as integer IDs
      fixture_int = Zlib.crc32("fixtures/#{label}") % (2**30 - 1)

      # Translate the deterministic order into times in the past, so that records
      # created during test runs are also always newer than the fixtures.
      base_time = Time.utc(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
      timestamp = base_time + (fixture_int / 1000.0)

      uuid_v7_with_timestamp(timestamp, label)
    end

    def uuid_v7_with_timestamp(time, seed_string)
      # Generate UUIDv7 with custom timestamp and deterministic random bits
      # Format: 48-bit timestamp_ms | 12-bit sub_ms_precision | 4-bit version | 62-bit random

      time_ms = time.to_f * 1000
      timestamp_ms = time_ms.to_i

      # 48-bit timestamp (milliseconds since epoch)
      bytes = []
      bytes[0] = (timestamp_ms >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[1] = (timestamp_ms >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[2] = (timestamp_ms >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[3] = (timestamp_ms >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[4] = (timestamp_ms >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[5] = timestamp_ms & 0xff

      # Use the 12-bit rand_a field for sub-millisecond precision
      # Extract fractional milliseconds and convert to 12-bit value (0-4095)
      # This gives us ~0.244 microsecond precision
      frac_ms = time_ms - timestamp_ms
      sub_ms_precision = (frac_ms * 4096).to_i & 0xfff

      # Derive deterministic "random" bits from seed_string for the remaining random bits
      hash = Digest::MD5.hexdigest(seed_string)

      # 12-bit sub-ms precision + 4-bit version (0111 for v7)
      bytes[6] = ((sub_ms_precision >> 8) & 0x0f) | 0x70  # version 7
      bytes[7] = sub_ms_precision & 0xff

      # 2-bit variant (10) + 62-bit random
      rand_b = hash[3...19].to_i(16) & ((2**62) - 1)
      bytes[8] = ((rand_b >> 56) & 0x3f) | 0x80  # variant 10
      bytes[9] = (rand_b >> 48) & 0xff
      bytes[10] = (rand_b >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[11] = (rand_b >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[12] = (rand_b >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[13] = (rand_b >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[14] = (rand_b >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[15] = rand_b & 0xff

      # Format as UUID string and convert to base36 (25 chars)
      uuid = "%02x%02x%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x" % bytes

class ApplicationJob < ActiveJob::Base
  prepend AccountTenanted

  # Automatically retry jobs that encountered a deadlock
  # retry_on ActiveRecord::Deadlocked

  # Most jobs are safe to ignore if the underlying records are no longer available
  # discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError
end
=== account_tenanted.rb ===
# Serializes the current account into job data so that jobs run
# within the correct account context via Current.with_account.
#
# Account resolution is deferred to an around_perform callback so
# that missing accounts raise DeserializationError inside the
# execution path where discard_on can handle it.
module AccountTenanted
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  prepended do
    attr_reader :account
    around_perform :with_account_context
  end

  def initialize(...)
    super
    @account = Current.account
  end

  def serialize
    super.merge({ "account" => @account&.to_gid })
  end

  def deserialize(job_data)
    super
    @account_gid = job_data["account"]
  end

  private
    def with_account_context(&block)
      resolve_account!

      if account.present?
        Current.with_account(account, &block)
      else
        yield
      end
    end

    def resolve_account!
      if @account_gid
        @account = GlobalID::Locator.locate(@account_gid)
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
      raise ActiveJob::DeserializationError
    end
end

module Card::Entropic
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    scope :postponing_soon, -> do
      now = Time.now
      active
        .joins(board: :account)
        .left_outer_joins(board: :entropy)
        .joins("LEFT OUTER JOIN entropies AS account_entropies ON account_entropies.account_id = accounts.id AND account_entropies.container_type = 'Account' AND account_entropies.container_id = accounts.id")
        .where("last_active_at > #{connection.date_subtract('?', 'COALESCE(entropies.auto_postpone_period, account_entropies.auto_postpone_period)')}", now)
        .where("last_active_at <= #{connection.date_subtract('?', 'COALESCE(entropies.auto_postpone_period, account_entropies.auto_postpone_period) * 0.75')}", now)
    end

    delegate :auto_postpone_period, to: :board
  end

  class_methods do
    # Iterates per account, grouping the account's boards by their effective
    # auto-postpone period (board override, else account default). Each group
    # queries with a single constant cutoff, so `account_id = ? AND
    # last_active_at <= ?` rides the existing index instead of computing the
    # threshold per row across every card in the system.
    def auto_postpone_all_due(as_of: Time.now)
      Account.find_each do |account|
        account.boards.includes(:entropy).group_by(&:auto_postpone_period).each do |period, boards|
          account.cards.active
            .where(board_id: boards.map(&:id))
            .where(last_active_at: ..(as_of - period))
            .find_each do |card|
              card.auto_postpone(user: account.system_user)
            end
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def entropy
    Card::Entropy.for(self)
  end

  def entropic?
    entropy.present?
  end
end

class Account::Import < ApplicationRecord
  broadcasts_refreshes

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :identity

  has_one_attached :file

  enum :status, %w[ pending processing completed failed ].index_by(&:itself), default: :pending
  enum :failure_reason, %w[ conflict invalid_export ].index_by(&:itself), prefix: :failed_due_to, scopes: false

  scope :expired, -> { where(completed_at: ...24.hours.ago).or(where(status: :failed, created_at: ...7.days.ago)) }

  def self.cleanup
    expired.each(&:cleanup)
  end

  def process_later
    Account::DataImportJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def check(start: nil, callback: nil)
    processing!

    ZipFile.read_from(file.blob) do |zip|
      Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new(account).each_record_set(start: start) do |record_set, last_id|
        record_set.check(from: zip, start: last_id, callback: callback)
      end
    end
  rescue Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet::ConflictError => e
    mark_as_failed(:conflict)
    raise e
  rescue Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet::IntegrityError, ZipFile::InvalidFileError => e
    mark_as_failed(:invalid_export)
    raise e
  rescue => e
    mark_as_failed
    raise e
  end

  def process(start: nil, callback: nil)
    processing!

    ZipFile.read_from(file.blob) do |zip|
      Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new(account).each_record_set(start: start) do |record_set, last_id|
        record_set.import(from: zip, start: last_id, callback: callback)
      end
    end

    add_importer_to_all_access_boards
    reconcile_cards_count
    reconcile_account_storage

    mark_completed
  rescue Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet::ConflictError => e
    mark_as_failed(:conflict)
    raise e
  rescue Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet::IntegrityError, ZipFile::InvalidFileError => e
    mark_as_failed(:invalid_export)
    raise e
  rescue => e
    mark_as_failed
    raise e
  end

  def cleanup
    destroy
    account.destroy if failed?
  end

  private
    def mark_completed
      update!(status: :completed, completed_at: Time.current)
      ImportMailer.completed(identity, account).deliver_later
    end

    def mark_as_failed(failure_reason = nil)
      update!(status: :failed, failure_reason: failure_reason)
      ImportMailer.failed(self).deliver_later
    end

    def reconcile_cards_count
      account.update_column :cards_count, [ account.cards_count, account.cards.maximum(:number).to_i ].max
    end

    def add_importer_to_all_access_boards
      importer = account.users.find_by!(identity: identity)

      account.boards.all_access.find_each do |board|
        board.accesses.grant_to(importer)
      end
    end

    def reconcile_account_storage
      account.boards.each(&:reconcile_storage)
      account.reconcile_storage
      account.materialize_storage
    end
end

# which skips attachment callbacks. We need `destroy` so storage ledger detaches
# are recorded and reused blobs (ActionText embeds) aren't purged until the
# last attachment is gone. Keep this local to Fizzy; it's not a Rails default.
module ActiveStorage
  module PurgeOnLastAttachment
    def purge
      @purge_mode = :purge
      destroy
      purge_blob_if_last(:purge) if destroyed?
    ensure
      @purge_mode = nil
    end

    def purge_later
      @purge_mode = :purge_later
      destroy
      purge_blob_if_last(:purge_later) if destroyed?
    ensure
      @purge_mode = nil
    end

    private
      # Rails registers `after_destroy_commit :purge_dependent_blob` (renamed from
      # `purge_dependent_blob_later` upstream, which also now handles dependent: :purge).
      # Override the current callback name so reused blobs (ActionText embeds) are only
      # purged once the last attachment is gone, and skip when an explicit purge/purge_later
      # is already driving the blob purge via `purge_blob_if_last` (@purge_mode set).
      def purge_dependent_blob
        return if @purge_mode

        # `record.nil?` must be checked first: `dependent` reads `record.attachment_reflections`,
        # so it can't be evaluated for an orphaned attachment — an absent record falls back to
        # purge_later.
        if record.nil? || dependent == :purge_later
          purge_blob_if_last(:purge_later)
        elsif dependent == :purge
          purge_blob_if_last(:purge)
        end
      end

      def purge_blob_if_last(mode)
        if blob && !blob.attachments.exists?
          mode == :purge ? blob.purge : blob.purge_later
        end
      end
  end
end

module Board::Storage
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include Storage::Totaled

  # Board's own embeds (public_description) count toward itself
  def board_for_storage_tracking
    self
  end

  private
    BATCH_SIZE = 1000

    # Calculate actual storage by summing blob sizes.
    #
    # Storage tracking is a business abstraction - we count what users upload.
    # Original upload bytes only; variants/previews/derivatives excluded.
    # Physical storage optimizations (deduplication, compression) don't affect quotas.
    def calculate_real_storage_bytes
      @card_ids = nil  # Clear memoization for fresh calculation
      card_image_bytes + card_embed_bytes + comment_embed_bytes + board_embed_bytes
    end

    def card_ids
      @card_ids ||= cards.ids
    end

    def card_image_bytes
      sum_blob_bytes_in_batches \
        ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(record_type: "Card", name: "image"),
        card_ids
    end

    def card_embed_bytes
      sum_embed_bytes_for "Card", card_ids
    end

    def comment_embed_bytes
      card_ids.each_slice(BATCH_SIZE).sum do |batch|
        sum_embed_bytes_for "Comment", Comment.where(card_id: batch).ids
      end
    end

    def board_embed_bytes
      sum_embed_bytes_for "Board", [ id ]
    end

    def sum_embed_bytes_for(record_type, record_ids)
      rich_text_ids = ActionText::RichText \
        .where(record_type: record_type, record_id: record_ids).ids

      sum_blob_bytes_in_batches \
        ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(record_type: "ActionText::RichText", name: "embeds"),
        rich_text_ids
    end

    def sum_blob_bytes_in_batches(base_scope, record_ids)
      # Count per-attachment to match ledger model.
      # Same blob attached 3 times = 3x bytes (business abstraction, not physical storage).
      #
      # Do NOT remove the join thinking it's a performance optimization - it's required
      # for correct per-attachment counting. We keep ActiveStorage/ActionText in the same
      # database (realm/geo partitioning, not functionality partitioning), so cross-table
      # joins are fine.
      record_ids.each_slice(BATCH_SIZE).sum do |batch_ids|
        base_scope
          .where(record_id: batch_ids)
          .joins(:blob)
          .sum("active_storage_blobs.byte_size")
      end
    end
end

module Storage::Totaled
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_one :storage_total, as: :owner, class_name: "Storage::Total", dependent: :destroy
    has_many :storage_entries, class_name: "Storage::Entry", foreign_key: foreign_key_for_storage
  end

  class_methods do
    def foreign_key_for_storage
      "#{model_name.singular}_id"
    end
  end

  # Fast: materialized snapshot (may be slightly stale)
  def bytes_used
    storage_total&.bytes_stored || 0
  end

  # Exact: snapshot + pending entries
  def bytes_used_exact
    create_or_find_storage_total.current_usage
  end

  def materialize_storage_later
    Storage::MaterializeJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  # Materialize all pending entries into snapshot
  def materialize_storage
    total = create_or_find_storage_total

    total.with_lock do
      latest_entry_id = storage_entries.maximum(:id)

      if latest_entry_id && total.last_entry_id != latest_entry_id
        scope = storage_entries.where(id: ..latest_entry_id)
        scope = scope.where.not(id: ..total.last_entry_id) if total.last_entry_id
        delta_sum = scope.sum(:delta)

        total.update! bytes_stored: total.bytes_stored + delta_sum, last_entry_id: latest_entry_id
      end
    end
  end

  # Reconcile ledger against actual attachment storage.
  #
  # Uses two-cursor approach for consistency: capture cursor before AND after the
  # scan. If they differ, entries were added during the scan and we can't get an
  # accurate diff without risking double-counting or undercounting.
  #
  # Returns true if reconciled successfully, false if aborted due to concurrent
  # writes. Caller (ReconcileJob) handles retries to avoid amplification.
  def reconcile_storage
    cursor_before = storage_entries.maximum(:id)
    real_bytes = calculate_real_storage_bytes
    cursor_after = storage_entries.maximum(:id)

    if cursor_before != cursor_after
      Rails.logger.warn "[Storage] Reconcile aborted for #{self.class}##{id}: cursor moved during scan"
      false
    else
      ledger_bytes = cursor_after ? storage_entries.where(id: ..cursor_after).sum(:delta) : 0
      diff = real_bytes - ledger_bytes

      if diff.nonzero?
        Rails.logger.info "[Storage] Reconcile #{self.class}##{id}: adjusting by #{diff} bytes"
        Storage::Entry.record \
          account: is_a?(Account) ? self : account,
          board: is_a?(Board) ? self : nil,
          recordable: nil,
          delta: diff,
          operation: "reconcile"
      end

      true
    end
  end

  private
    def create_or_find_storage_total
      self.storage_total ||= Storage::Total.create_or_find_by!(owner: self)
    end

    def calculate_real_storage_bytes
      raise NotImplementedError, "Subclass must implement calculate_real_storage_bytes"
    end
end

# Enforce storage ledger integrity by preventing blob reuse in tracked contexts.
#
# Two invariants:
# 1. Account match: blob.account_id == record.account_id (multi-tenant safety)
# 2. No reuse within tracked contexts: a blob can only have one tracked attachment
#
# With per-attachment reconcile, blob reuse inside an account wouldn't break correctness -
# ledger would still count each attach, and reconcile would agree. However, we intentionally
# forbid reuse (except templates) as a product/control decision:
# - Simpler mental model (one blob = one attachment)
# - Prevents accidental quota manipulation via direct blob_id reuse
# - Cleaner audit trail in ledger entries
#
# Scope note: The no-reuse validation only blocks reuse when the *new* attachment is tracked
# AND only checks *existing* attachments in Storage::TRACKED_RECORD_TYPES. A blob first
# attached to an untracked type (avatar/export) could theoretically be reused in a tracked
# context. This is acceptable - user-accessible blob IDs from untracked contexts are
# basically nonexistent in practice.
#
# Exception: ActionText embeds are allowed to reuse blobs to support copy/paste.

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_storage_attachment) do
  validate :blob_account_matches_record, on: :create
  validate :no_tracked_blob_reuse, on: :create

  private
    # Multi-tenant safety: blob must belong to same account as record
    # NOTE: Skips validation if record.account is nil. This is a theoretical bypass
    # if someone attaches before account assignment, but our flows assign account
    # before attachment. Global/unaccounted attachments (Identity/User avatars, exports)
    # bypass tenancy checks via try(:account) returning nil - this is intentional as
    # these classes don't participate in storage tracking.
    def blob_account_matches_record
      if record&.try(:account).present? && !whitelisted_for_cross_account?
        unless blob&.account_id == record.account.id
          errors.add(:blob_id, "blob account must match record account")
        end
      end
    end

    # Ledger integrity: blob can only have one tracked attachment
    def no_tracked_blob_reuse
      tracked_record = record&.try(:storage_tracked_record)
      if tracked_record.present? &&
          !whitelisted_for_cross_account? &&
          !(record_type == "ActionText::RichText" && name == "embeds")

        # Check for existing attachment of this blob in tracked contexts
        # Uses Storage::TRACKED_RECORD_TYPES constant to stay generic
        existing = ActiveStorage::Attachment
          .where(blob_id: blob_id)
          .where(record_type: Storage::TRACKED_RECORD_TYPES)
          .where.not(id: id)
          .exists?

        if existing
          errors.add(:blob_id, "cannot reuse blob in tracked storage context")
        end
      end
    end

    def whitelisted_for_cross_account?
      # Only template account blobs can be reused cross-tenant.
      # When TEMPLATE_ACCOUNT_ID is nil, no exemptions are granted.
      Storage::TEMPLATE_ACCOUNT_ID.present? && blob&.account_id == Storage::TEMPLATE_ACCOUNT_ID
    end
end

module Account::StorageLimited
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT = 1.gigabyte
  NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 500.megabytes

  included do
    has_one :storage_exception
  end

  def storage_limit
    storage_exception&.bytes_allowed || DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT
  end

  def exceeding_storage_limit?
    bytes_used > storage_limit
  end

  def nearing_storage_limit?
    !exceeding_storage_limit? && bytes_used > storage_limit - NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end

  def add_storage_exception(bytes)
    if storage_exception
      storage_exception.update!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    else
      create_storage_exception!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    end
  end

  class InvalidFileError < StandardError; end

  class << self
    def create_for(attachment, filename:)
      raise ArgumentError, "No block given" unless block_given?

      reflection = attachment.record.class.reflect_on_attachment(attachment.name)
      service_name = reflection.options[:service_name] || ActiveStorage::Blob.service.name
      service = ActiveStorage::Blob.services.fetch(service_name)

      if s3_service?(service)
        create_for_s3(attachment, filename: filename, service: service) { |zip| yield zip }
      else
        create_for_disk(attachment, filename: filename) { |zip| yield zip }
      end
    end

    def read_from(blob)
      raise ArgumentError, "No block given" unless block_given?

      if s3_service?(blob.service)
        read_from_s3(blob) { |zip| yield zip }
      else
        read_from_disk(blob) { |zip| yield zip }
      end
    end

    private
      def s3_service?(service)
        # The S3 service doesn't get loaded in development unless it's used
        defined?(ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service) && service.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service)
      end

      def create_for_s3(attachment, filename:, service:)
        blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_before_direct_upload!(
          filename: filename,
          content_type: "application/zip",
          byte_size: 0,
          checksum: "pending"
        )

        writer = Writer.new

        # Use S3's upload_stream directly for write-based streaming.
        # ActiveStorage's upload method expects a read-based IO, but ZipKit
        # needs a write-based stream. The TransferManager's upload_stream
        # yields a writable IO that we can stream directly to.
        service.send(:upload_stream,
          key: blob.key,
          content_type: "application/zip",
          part_size: 100.megabytes
        ) do |write_stream|
          write_stream.binmode
          writer.stream_to(write_stream)
          yield writer
          writer.close
        end

        blob.update!(byte_size: writer.byte_size, checksum: writer.checksum)
        attachment.attach(blob)
      rescue Aws::S3::MultipartUploadError => e
        if e.errors.any?
          raise e.errors.first
        else
          raise e
        end
      end

      def create_for_disk(attachment, filename:)
        tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "export", ".zip" ])
        tempfile.binmode

        writer = Writer.new(tempfile)
        yield writer
        writer.close

        tempfile.rewind
        attachment.attach(io: tempfile, filename: filename, content_type: "application/zip")
      ensure
        tempfile&.close
        tempfile&.unlink
      end

      def read_from_s3(blob)
        url = blob.url(expires_in: 6.hour)
        ssl_verify_peer = blob.service.client.client.config.ssl_verify_peer
        remote_io = RemoteIO.new(url, ssl_verify_peer: ssl_verify_peer)
        reader = Reader.new(remote_io)
        yield reader
      end

      def read_from_disk(blob)
        blob.open do |file|
          reader = Reader.new(file)
          yield reader
        end
      end

# Serializes the current account into job data so that jobs run
# within the correct account context via Current.with_account.
#
# Account resolution is deferred to an around_perform callback so
# that missing accounts raise DeserializationError inside the
# execution path where discard_on can handle it.
module AccountTenanted
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  prepended do
    attr_reader :account
    around_perform :with_account_context
  end

  def initialize(...)
    super
    @account = Current.account
  end

  def serialize
    super.merge({ "account" => @account&.to_gid })
  end

  def deserialize(job_data)
    super
    @account_gid = job_data["account"]
  end

  private
    def with_account_context(&block)
      resolve_account!

      if account.present?
        Current.with_account(account, &block)
      else
        yield
      end
    end

    def resolve_account!
      if @account_gid
        @account = GlobalID::Locator.locate(@account_gid)
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
      raise ActiveJob::DeserializationError
    end
end

module SmtpDeliveryErrorHandling
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    # Retry delivery to possibly-unavailable remote mailservers.
    retry_on Net::OpenTimeout, Net::ReadTimeout, Socket::ResolutionError, wait: :polynomially_longer

    # Net::SMTPServerBusy is SMTP error code 4xx, a temporary error.
    # Common one we've seen is 452 4.3.1 Insufficient system storage.
    # Patiently retry.
    retry_on Net::SMTPServerBusy, wait: :polynomially_longer

    # SMTP error 50x.
    rescue_from Net::SMTPSyntaxError do |error|
      case error.message
      when /\A501 5\.1\.3/
        # Ignore undeliverable email addresses.
        Sentry.capture_exception error, level: :info if Fizzy.saas?
      else
        raise
      end
    end

    # SMTP error 5xx except 50x and 53x.
    # * 550 5.1.1: Unknown users
    # * 552 5.6.0: Message/headers too large
    rescue_from Net::SMTPFatalError do |error|
      case error.message
      when /\A550 5\.1\.1/, /\A552 5\.6\.0/, /\A555 5\.5\.4/
        Sentry.capture_exception error, level: :info if Fizzy.saas?
      else
        raise
      end
    end
  end
end

# Repair task — reindexes every searchable Card and Comment in the database.
# Intended to be invoked manually after a search-index loss event. Not a recurring job.
#
# Idempotent: Searchable#reindex upserts by (searchable_type, searchable_id).
# Continuable: if the worker is interrupted, the job resumes from the last-processed id.
#
# `rich_text_limit` is a safety valve against unbounded bodies: records whose rich text
# exceeds the limit (in bytes) are filtered out at the SQL level, so they never materialize
# in Ruby. Without it, a single pathological body can stall the batch query or OOM the
# worker during preload, which has happened in practice.
#
# Usage:
#   SearchReindexJob.perform_later
#   SearchReindexJob.perform_later(batch_size: 500, log_every: 100, rich_text_limit: 50_000)
class SearchReindexJob < ApplicationJob
  include ActiveJob::Continuable

  queue_as :backend

  def perform(batch_size: 100, log_every: 1000, rich_text_limit: 100_000)
    step :cards do |step|
      processed = 0
      Card.published
          .left_joins(:rich_text_description)
          .where("action_text_rich_texts.body IS NULL OR OCTET_LENGTH(action_text_rich_texts.body) <= ?", rich_text_limit)
          .includes(:rich_text_description)
          .find_each(start: step.cursor, batch_size: batch_size) do |card|
        safely_reindex(card)
        processed += 1
        log_progress(:cards, processed, card.id) if (processed % log_every).zero?
        step.advance! from: card.id
      end
    end

    step :comments do |step|
      processed = 0
      Comment.joins(:card).merge(Card.published)
             .left_joins(:rich_text_body)
             .where("action_text_rich_texts.body IS NULL OR OCTET_LENGTH(action_text_rich_texts.body) <= ?", rich_text_limit)
             .includes(:rich_text_body, :card)
             .find_each(start: step.cursor, batch_size: batch_size) do |comment|
        safely_reindex(comment)
        processed += 1
        log_progress(:comments, processed, comment.id) if (processed % log_every).zero?
        step.advance! from: comment.id
      end
    end
  end

  private
    def safely_reindex(record)
      record.reindex
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.error.report(e, context: { record_type: record.class.name, record_id: record.id })
    end

    def log_progress(step_name, count, cursor)
      Rails.logger.info { "SearchReindexJob: step=#{step_name} processed=#{count} cursor=#{cursor}" }
    end
end

module Board::Accessible
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :delete_all do
      def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
        transaction do
          grant_to granted
          revoke_from revoked
        end
      end

      def grant_to(users)
        Access.insert_all Array(users).collect { |user| { id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, board_id: proxy_association.owner.id, user_id: user.id, account_id: proxy_association.owner.account.id } }
      end

      def revoke_from(users)
        destroy_by user: users unless proxy_association.owner.all_access?
      end
    end

    has_many :users, through: :accesses
    has_many :access_only_users, -> { merge(Access.access_only) }, through: :accesses, source: :user

    scope :all_access, -> { where(all_access: true) }

    after_create :grant_access_to_creator
    after_save_commit :grant_access_to_everyone
  end

  def accessed_by(user)
    access_for(user).accessed
  end

  def access_for(user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def accessible_to?(user)
    access_for(user).present?
  end

  def clean_inaccessible_data_for(user)
    return if accessible_to?(user)

    mentions_for_user(user).destroy_all
    notifications_for_user(user).destroy_all
    watches_for(user).destroy_all
    pins_for(user).destroy_all
  end

  def watchers
    users.active.where(accesses: { involvement: :watching })
  end

  private
    def grant_access_to_creator
      accesses.create(user: creator, involvement: :watching)
    end

    def grant_access_to_everyone
      accesses.grant_to(account.users.active) if all_access_previously_changed?(to: true)
    end

    def mentions_for_user(user)
      # Query handles 2 paths:
      #
      # 1. Mention->Card
      # 2. Mention->Comment->Card
      board_id_binary = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(id)

      user.mentions
        .joins("LEFT JOIN cards ON mentions.source_id = cards.id AND mentions.source_type = 'Card'")
        .joins("LEFT JOIN comments ON mentions.source_id = comments.id AND mentions.source_type = 'Comment'")
        .joins("LEFT JOIN cards AS comment_cards ON comments.card_id = comment_cards.id")
        .where("(mentions.source_type = 'Card' AND cards.board_id = ?) OR (mentions.source_type = 'Comment' AND comment_cards.board_id = ?)", board_id_binary, board_id_binary)
    end

    def notifications_for_user(user)
      # Query handles 2 paths:
      #
      # 1. Notification->Event->Card
      # 2. Notification->Event->Comment->Card
      #
      # Notification->Event->Mention->Card and Notification->Event->Mention->Comment->Card are
      # handled by destroying mentions_for_user.
      uuid_type = ActiveRecord::Type.lookup(:uuid, adapter: :trilogy)
      board_id_binary = uuid_type.serialize(id)

class User::DataExport < Export

    end

      exportable_cards.find_each do |card|

      end
    end

    def exportable_cards
      user.accessible_cards.includes(
        :board,
        creator: :identity,
        comments: { creator: :identity },
        rich_text_description: { embeds_attachments: :blob }
      )
    end

    def add_card_to_zip(zip, card)
      zip.add_file("#{card.number}.json", card.export_json)

      card.export_attachments.each do |attachment|
        zip.add_file(attachment[:path], compress: false) do |f|
          attachment[:blob].download { |chunk| f.write(chunk) }
        end
      rescue ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError
        # Skip attachments where the file is missing from storage
      end
    end
end

  belongs_to :account

  def redeem_if(&block)
    with_lock do
      increment!(:usage_count) if active? && block.call(account)
    end
  end

  def active?
    usage_count < usage_limit
  end

  def reset
    generate_code
    self.usage_count = 0
    save!
  end

    def generate_code
      self.code = loop do
        candidate = SecureRandom.base58(CODE_LENGTH).scan(/.{4}/).join("-")
        break candidate unless self.class.exists?(code: candidate)
      end
    end

class Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::FileRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::ActiveStorage::Blob)
  end

  private
    def records
      ::ActiveStorage::Blob.where(account: account).where.not(id: excluded_blob_ids)
    end

    def excluded_blob_ids
      ::ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(account: account, record_type: INTERNAL_RECORD_TYPES).select(:blob_id)
    end

    def export_record(blob)
      if blob.service.exist?(blob.key)
        zip.add_file("storage/#{blob.key}", compress: false) do |out|
          blob.download { |chunk| out.write(chunk) }
        end
      end
    end

    def files
      zip.glob("storage/*")
    end

    def import_batch(files)
      files.each do |file|
        old_key = file.delete_prefix("storage/")
        blob_id = old_key_to_blob_id[old_key]
        raise IntegrityError, "Storage file #{old_key} has no matching blob metadata in export" unless blob_id

        blob = ::ActiveStorage::Blob.find_by(id: blob_id, account: account)
        raise IntegrityError, "Blob #{blob_id} not found for storage key #{old_key}" unless blob

        zip.read(file) do |stream|
          blob.upload(stream)
        end
      end
    end

    def old_key_to_blob_id
      @old_key_to_blob_id ||= build_old_key_to_blob_id
    end

    def build_old_key_to_blob_id
      zip.glob("data/active_storage_blobs/*.json").each_with_object({}) do |file, map|
        data = load(file)
        old_key = data["key"]
        if map.key?(old_key)
          raise IntegrityError, "Duplicate blob key in export: #{old_key}"
        end
        map[old_key] = data["id"]
      end
    end

    def with_zip(zip)
      @old_key_to_blob_id = nil
      super
    end

    def check_record(file_path)
      old_key = file_path.delete_prefix("storage/")

      unless old_key_to_blob_id.key?(old_key)
        raise IntegrityError, "Storage file #{old_key} has no matching blob metadata in export"
      end
    end

require "zlib"

module User::Avatar
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  ALLOWED_AVATAR_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ image/jpeg image/png image/gif image/webp ].freeze
  MAX_AVATAR_DIMENSIONS = { width: 4096, height: 4096 }.freeze
  AVATAR_COLORS = %w[
    #AF2E1B #CC6324 #3B4B59 #BFA07A #ED8008 #ED3F1C #BF1B1B #736B1E #D07B53
    #736356 #AD1D1D #BF7C2A #C09C6F #698F9C #7C956B #5D618F #3B3633 #67695E
  ].freeze

  included do
    has_one_attached :avatar do |attachable|
      attachable.variant :thumb, resize_to_fill: [ 256, 256 ], process: :immediately
    end

    scope :with_avatars, -> { preload(:account, :avatar_attachment) }

    validate :avatar_content_type_allowed, :avatar_dimensions_allowed, if: :avatar_attached?
  end

  def avatar_attached?
    avatar.attached?
  end

  def avatar_thumbnail
    avatar.variable? ? avatar.variant(:thumb) : avatar
  end

  def avatar_background_color
    AVATAR_COLORS[Zlib.crc32(to_param) % AVATAR_COLORS.size]
  end

  # Avatars are always publicly accessible
  def publicly_accessible?
    true
  end

  private
    def avatar_content_type_allowed
      unless ALLOWED_AVATAR_CONTENT_TYPES.include?(avatar.content_type)
        errors.add(:avatar, "must be a JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP image")
      end
    end

    def avatar_dimensions_allowed
      return unless avatar.blob.analyzed? || avatar.blob.analyze

      width = avatar.blob.metadata[:width]
      height = avatar.blob.metadata[:height]

      if width && width > MAX_AVATAR_DIMENSIONS[:width]
        errors.add(:avatar, "width must be less than #{MAX_AVATAR_DIMENSIONS[:width]}px")
      end

      if height && height > MAX_AVATAR_DIMENSIONS[:height]
        errors.add(:avatar, "height must be less than #{MAX_AVATAR_DIMENSIONS[:height]}px")
      end
    end
end

module User::Notifiable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :notifications, dependent: :destroy
    has_many :notification_bundles, class_name: "Notification::Bundle", dependent: :destroy

    generates_token_for :unsubscribe, expires_in: 1.month
  end

  def bundle(notification)
    with_lock do
      find_or_create_bundle_for(notification)
    end
  end

  private
    def find_or_create_bundle_for(notification)
      find_bundle_for(notification) || expand_pending_bundle_for(notification) || create_bundle_for(notification)
    end

    def find_bundle_for(notification)
      notification_bundles.pending.containing(notification).last
    end

    def expand_pending_bundle_for(notification)
      pending = notification_bundles.pending.last
      if pending.present? && notification.updated_at < pending.starts_at
        pending.update!(starts_at: notification.updated_at) # expand the window to include this notification
      end
    end

    def create_bundle_for(notification)
      notification_bundles.create!(starts_at: notification.updated_at)
    end
end

steps.message: Let me run the diagnostic on a freshly created account (with `after_destroy_commit` running properly) to see every single record left behind and every job enqueued when calling `account.destroy!`.
steps.reasoning_content:
**Analyzing Push Endpoint Behavior and Transactional Integrity**

Okay, so I need to thoroughly understand how this push endpoint, let's say a Firebase Cloud Messaging URL like `https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/1`, behaves. I'm going to test it rigorously, particularly focusing on what happens after a database transaction commits, and also what happens if we're inside a test or a rolled-back transaction. Wait, I have to remember that `after_destroy_commit` callbacks are triggered *only* after a successful commit. That's a crucial detail. That means, running this code within a transaction that's then rolled back, will skip callbacks like `remove_from_search_index` and `purge_dependent_blob`, and this needs to be part of the test.

So, the plan is to check the push endpoint behavior both with and without the transaction committing. To do this comprehensively, I'll either spin up a completely fresh account in the test environment, or I'll run this inside a mini test script that handles its own cleanup. This way, I can isolate the behavior and inspect it without any lingering dependencies. I'm thinking, creating a new account should be the best approach for a clean test.

arguments.command:
RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails runner '
ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = :test
ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter.enqueued_jobs.clear

identity = Identity.find_or_create_by!(email_address: "diag_test_incinerate@example.com")
account = Account.create_with_owner(account: { name: "Diag Account" }, owner: { name: "Diag Owner", identity: identity })
account_id = account.id
user = account.users.owner.first
member = account.users.create!(name: "Diag Member", role: :member)

Current.set(account: account, user: user) do
  board = account.boards.create!(name: "Diag Board", creator: user, all_access: true)
  board.update!(public_description: "Public desc")
  board.publish
  board.create_entropy!(auto_postpone_period: 7.days, account: account)
  col = board.columns.create!(name: "Col 1", color: Color::COLORS.first)
  tag = account.tags.create!(title: "diag-tag")
  card = board.cards.create!(title: "Diag Card", creator: user, status: :published, column: col, description: "Card desc")
  card.image.attach(io: StringIO.new("card image data"), filename: "card.png", content_type: "image/png")
  card.toggle_tag_with("diag-tag")
  card.assign(member, assigner: user)
  card.steps.create!(content: "Step 1")
  card.pin_by(user)
  card.gild
  card.reactions.create!(content: "👍", reacter: user)
  comment = card.comments.create!(body: "Hello comment", creator: user)
  comment.reactions.create!(content: "🎉", reacter: member)
  Mention.create!(account: account, source: comment, mentioner: user, mentionee: member)
  card.close(user: user)
  card.postpone(user: user)
  card.create_activity_spike!(account: account)
  webhook = board.webhooks.create!(name: "Hook", url: "https://example.com/hook", subscribed_actions: ["card_published"])
  webhook.deliveries.create!(account: account, event: card.events.first, state: "completed")
  user.filters.create!(fields: { indexed_by: "all" }, boards: [board], tags: [tag], assignees: [member], creators: [user], closers: [user])
  user.remember_search("diag search")
  user.push_subscriptions.create!(endpoint: "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/diag123", p256dh_key: "key", auth_key: "auth")
  user.avatar.attach(io: StringIO.new("fake"), filename: "a.png", content_type: "image/png") rescue nil
  ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(io: StringIO.new("orphan blob"), filename: "orphan.txt", content_type: "text/plain")
  export = Account::Export.create!(account: account, user: user)
  user_export = User::DataExport.create!(account: account, user: user)
  import = Account::Import.create!(account: account, identity: identity)
  Notification.create!(account: account, user: member, creator: user, source: card.events.first, card: card)
  Notification::Bundle.create!(account: account, user: member, starts_at: 1.hour.ago, ends_at: Time.current)
  Storage::Entry.record(account: account, board: board, delta: 1234, operation: "attach")
  account.materialize_storage
  board.materialize_storage
  account.cancel(initiated_by: user)
  card.reindex
  comment.reindex
end

board_ids = account.boards.ids
filter_ids = Filter.where(account_id: account_id).ids

def report(label, account_id, board_ids, filter_ids)
  puts "=== #{label} ==="
  conn = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
  conn.tables.sort.each do |table|
    cols = conn.columns(table).map(&:name)
    count = if cols.include?("account_id")
      conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM #{table} WHERE account_id = #{conn.quote(account_id)}")
    elsif table == "accounts"
      conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM accounts WHERE id = #{conn.quote(account_id)}")
    elsif table == "storage_totals"
      ids = [account_id] + board_ids
      conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM storage_totals WHERE owner_id IN (#{ids.map { |i| conn.quote(i) }.join(",")})")
    elsif table.end_with?("_filters") || table == "filters_tags"
      if filter_ids.any?
        conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM #{table} WHERE filter_id IN (#{filter_ids.map { |i| conn.quote(i) }.join(",")})")
      else
        0
      end
    elsif table == "search_records_fts"
      conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_records_fts WHERE rowid NOT IN (SELECT id FROM search_records)")
    else
      next
    end
    puts "  #{table}: #{count}" if count.to_i > 0
  end
end

report("BEFORE DESTROY", account_id, board_ids, filter_ids)
ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter.enqueued_jobs.clear

account.destroy!

report("AFTER DESTROY (BEFORE ENQUEUED JOBS)", account_id, board_ids, filter_ids)
puts "=== ENQUEUED JOBS DURING DESTROY ==="
ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter.enqueued_jobs.each do |j|
  puts "  #{j["job_class"]} args=#{j["arguments"].inspect}"
end

# Clean up our leftover test data
ActiveRecord::Base.connection.tables.each do |t|
  cols = ActiveRecord::Base.connection.columns(t).map(&:name)
  if cols.include?("account_id")
    ActiveRecord::Base.connection.execute("DELETE FROM #{t} WHERE account_id = #{ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(account_id)}")
  end
end
identity.destroy!
'

steps.message: Let me bypass SSRF validation for the diagnostic push subscription creation so the script runs cleanly offline.
steps.reasoning_content:
Okay, here's my interpretation of that thought process, tailored for an expert audience, and written in the first person:

**SSR Fix: Offline DNS Bypass for Push Subscriptions**

Right, so DNS resolution is predictably a no-go in our offline SSRF check for that `push_subscription` flow. Aha, I see the path forward. Since we're facing an environment with limited external connectivity, the `save(validate: false)` trick is precisely what we need to bypass DNS validation during the creation of the `push_subscription` object. This way we can circumvent the check completely. No network, no problem. I can force the creation and, critically, push our diagnosis forward. Let's fire that diagnostic script off! Time to see if we've successfully sidestepped the dependency.

arguments.command:
RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails runner '
ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = :test
ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter.enqueued_jobs.clear

Account.where(name: "Diag Account").each do |a|
  aid = a.id
  ActiveRecord::Base.connection.tables.each do |t|
    cols = ActiveRecord::Base.connection.columns(t).map(&:name)
    ActiveRecord::Base.connection.execute("DELETE FROM #{t} WHERE account_id = #{ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(aid)}") if cols.include?("account_id")
  end
  a.delete
end
Identity.where(email_address: "diag_test_incinerate@example.com").destroy_all

identity = Identity.create!(email_address: "diag_test_incinerate@example.com")
account = Account.create_with_owner(account: { name: "Diag Account" }, owner: { name: "Diag Owner", identity: identity })
account_id = account.id
user = account.users.owner.first
member = account.users.create!(name: "Diag Member", role: :member)

Current.set(account: account, user: user) do
  board = account.boards.create!(name: "Diag Board", creator: user, all_access: true)
  board.update!(public_description: "Public desc")
  board.publish
  board.create_entropy!(auto_postpone_period: 7.days, account: account)
  col = board.columns.create!(name: "Col 1", color: Color::COLORS.first)
  tag = account.tags.create!(title: "diag-tag")
  card = board.cards.create!(title: "Diag Card", creator: user, status: :published, column: col, description: "Card desc")
  card.image.attach(io: StringIO.new("card image data"), filename: "card.png", content_type: "image/png")
  card.toggle_tag_with("diag-tag")
  card.assignments.create!(assignee: member, assigner: user)
  card.steps.create!(content: "Step 1")
  card.pin_by(user)
  card.gild
  card.reactions.create!(content: "👍", reacter: user)
  comment = card.comments.create!(body: "Hello comment", creator: user)
  comment.reactions.create!(content: "🎉", reacter: member)
  Mention.create!(account: account, source: comment, mentioner: user, mentionee: member)
  card.close(user: user)
  card.postpone(user: user)
  card.create_activity_spike!(account: account)
  webhook = board.webhooks.create!(name: "Hook", url: "https://example.com/hook", subscribed_actions: ["card_published"])
  webhook.deliveries.create!(account: account, event: card.events.first, state: "completed")
  user.filters.create!(fields: { indexed_by: "all" }, boards: [board], tags: [tag], assignees: [member], creators: [user], closers: [user])
  user.remember_search("diag search")
  ps = user.push_subscriptions.build(endpoint: "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/diag123", p256dh_key: "key", auth_key: "auth")
  ps.save!(validate: false)
  ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(io: StringIO.new("orphan blob"), filename: "orphan.txt", content_type: "text/plain")
  export = Account::Export.create!(account: account, user: user)
  export.file.attach(io: StringIO.new("export zip"), filename: "export.zip", content_type: "application/zip")
  user_export = User::DataExport.create!(account: account, user: user)
  user_export.file.attach(io: StringIO.new("uexport zip"), filename: "uexport.zip", content_type: "application/zip")
  import = Account::Import.create!(account: account, identity: identity)
  import.file.attach(io: StringIO.new("import zip"), filename: "import.zip", content_type: "application/zip")
  Notification.create!(account: account, user: member, creator: user, source: card.events.first, card: card)
  Notification::Bundle.create!(account: account, user: member, starts_at: 1.hour.ago, ends_at: Time.current)
  Storage::Entry.record(account: account, board: board, delta: 1234, operation: "attach")
  account.materialize_storage
  board.materialize_storage
  account.cancel(initiated_by: user)
  card.reindex
  comment.reindex
end

board_ids = account.boards.ids
filter_ids = Filter.where(account_id: account_id).ids

def report(label, account_id, board_ids, filter_ids)
  puts "=== #{label} ==="
  conn = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
  conn.tables.sort.each do |table|
    cols = conn.columns(table).map(&:name)
    count = if cols.include?("account_id")
      conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM #{table} WHERE account_id = #{conn.quote(account_id)}")
    elsif table == "accounts"
      conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM accounts WHERE id = #{conn.quote(account_id)}")
    elsif table == "storage_totals"
      ids = [account_id] + board_ids
      conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM storage_totals WHERE owner_id IN (#{ids.map { |i| conn.quote(i) }.join(",")})")
    elsif table.end_with?("_filters") || table == "filters_tags"
      if filter_ids.any?
        conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM #{table} WHERE filter_id IN (#{filter_ids.map { |i| conn.quote(i) }.join(",")})")
      else
        0
      end
    elsif table == "search_records_fts"
      conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_records_fts WHERE rowid NOT IN (SELECT id FROM search_records)")
    else
      next
    end
    puts "  #{table}: #{count}" if count.to_i > 0
  end
end

report("BEFORE DESTROY", account_id, board_ids, filter_ids)
ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter.enqueued_jobs.clear

account.destroy!

report("AFTER DESTROY (BEFORE ENQUEUED JOBS)", account_id, board_ids, filter_ids)
puts "=== ENQUEUED JOBS DURING DESTROY ==="
ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter.enqueued_jobs.each do |j|
  puts "  #{j["job_class"]} args=#{j["arguments"].inspect}"
end

# Clean up our leftover test data
ActiveRecord::Base.connection.tables.each do |t|
  cols = ActiveRecord::Base.connection.columns(t).map(&:name)
  if cols.include?("account_id")
    ActiveRecord::Base.connection.execute("DELETE FROM #{t} WHERE account_id = #{ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(account_id)}")
  end
end
identity.destroy!
'

steps.message: Running `account.destroy!` on a populated account immediately crashed with `Validation failed: Account must exist` inside `Storage::AttachmentTracking#record_storage_detach`! Let me inspect what was left behind in the database right now and what else `account.destroy!` does or misses.
steps.reasoning_content:
**A Deep Dive into a Deletion Disaster**

Whoa, hold on a second! Look at this crash we just stumbled upon right out of the gate! This stack trace is screaming at me: `Validation failed: Account must exist (ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid)`. It looks like it's happening during a `Storage::Entry.record` call within `Storage::AttachmentTracking#record_storage_detach`, and it's tied to an `account.destroy!` operation. What on earth is going on here?

Okay, let's break this down. First, the `card.image` is destroyed as part of the `account.destroy!` process. Then, in `Storage::AttachmentTracking#snapshot_storage_context`, we're creating a snapshot that includes the `account` associated with the "card". The key here is that `storage_tracked_record` (the card) is loading *its own* `Account` Ruby object instance (`card.account`). This instance is distinct from the `account` object we're actually calling `.destroy!` on.

So, here's the kicker. When `account.destroy!` finishes committing, the `account` Ruby object is destroyed (`account.destroyed? == true`). BUT, because `@storage_snapshot[:account]` is a *different* Ruby object instance, its destroyed status is false (`@storage_snapshot[:account].destroyed? == false`)! The `after_destroy_commit` then runs `Storage::AttachmentTracking#record_storage_detach` which calls `Storage::Entry.record`, passing that stale snapshot. `Storage::Entry.record` sensibly checks if the account is destroyed (`return if account.destroyed?`), but it's checking the *wrong* object! It thinks the account isn't destroyed, and then attempts to create an entry for an account that is already gone! Which leads to a database query to check that the account exists, and then the validation fails, and the application explodes!

That is a serious bug, and we just found it with a single diagnostic. This opens up a lot of questions. Let's see what else gets uncovered by running the full diagnostic, and handling that specific error. This is a chance to review the entire architecture!

module ActiveRecord
  module Type
    class Uuid < Binary
      BASE36_LENGTH = 25 # 36^25 > 2^128

      class << self
        def generate
          uuid = SecureRandom.uuid_v7
          hex = uuid.delete("-")
          hex_to_base36(hex)
        end

        def hex_to_base36(hex)
          hex.to_i(16).to_s(36).rjust(BASE36_LENGTH, "0")
        end

        def base36_to_hex(base36)
          base36.to_s.to_i(36).to_s(16).rjust(32, "0")
        end
      end

      def serialize(value)
        return unless value

        binary = Uuid.base36_to_hex(value).scan(/../).map(&:hex).pack("C*")

      end

      def deserialize(value)
        return unless value

        hex = value.to_s.unpack1("H*")
        Uuid.hex_to_base36(hex)
      end

      def cast(value)
        value
      end
    end
  end

module UuidPrimaryKeyDefault
  def load_schema!
    define_uuid_primary_key_pending_default
    super
  end

  private
    def define_uuid_primary_key_pending_default
      if uuid_primary_key?
        pending_attribute_modifications << PendingUuidDefault.new(primary_key)
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid
      # Table doesn't exist yet
    end

    def uuid_primary_key?
      table_name && primary_key && schema_cache.columns_hash(table_name)[primary_key]&.type == :uuid
    end

    PendingUuidDefault = Struct.new(:name) do
      def apply_to(attribute_set)
        attribute_set[name] = attribute_set[name].with_user_default(-> { ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate })
      end
    end
end

module MysqlUuidAdapter
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # Override lookup_cast_type to recognize binary(16) as UUID type
  def lookup_cast_type(sql_type)
    if sql_type == "binary(16)"
      ActiveRecord::Type.lookup(:uuid, adapter: :trilogy)
    else
      super
    end
  end

  # Override fetch_type_metadata to preserve UUID type and limit
  def fetch_type_metadata(sql_type, extra = "")
    if sql_type == "binary(16)"

        type: :uuid,
        limit: 16
      )
      ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::MySQL::TypeMetadata.new(simple_type, extra: extra)
    else
      super
    end
  end

  class_methods do
    def native_database_types
      @native_database_types_with_uuid ||= super.merge(uuid: { name: "binary", limit: 16 })

  end

  # Override lookup_cast_type to recognize BLOB as UUID type

    if sql_type == "blob(16)"
      ActiveRecord::Type.lookup(:uuid, adapter: :sqlite3)
    else
      super
    end

  # Override fetch_type_metadata to preserve UUID type and limit

    if sql_type == "blob(16)"

        type: :uuid,

  # Map binary(16) and blob(16) columns to :uuid type in schema.rb

    )

Okay, let's dissect this account incineration problem. The core is the `Account::IncinerateDueJob`, designed to scrub canceled account data after a 30-day grace period. The choice of hourly execution, as opposed to daily, offers a quicker turnaround for immediate account data removal when the 30-day window has expired, and also gracefully handles job interruptions or high volumes of due accounts. This has been confirmed via thorough reading of the documentation and prior patterns within the system.

Now, here's where it gets interesting: the synchronous versus asynchronous execution of the incineration. Based on the requirements and also my understanding, it is vital that `Account::IncinerateDueJob` *directly* executes the incineration logic. The job should *not* queue further per-account jobs. Why? Because the prompt specifies we need the data PERMANENTLY removed. The job needs to directly perform the work. By doing this in the same transaction, you would fail fast, and prevent orphaned records in case of any issue. This also helps with the creation of unit tests that would need to be very convoluted if the job was async.

Now, let's get into the *really* crucial part: data integrity and transaction management. `Account.incinerate_due` will iterate through eligible accounts and `account.incinerate` will be called for each of them. I think we should check an account's cancellability *within* the `incinerate` method to ensure that a race condition between `reactivate` and `incinerate` doesn't destroy an active account.

Given the potential size of the data associated with an account – which can be extremely large – we absolutely cannot wrap the entire incineration process in a single massive database transaction. This would lead to huge problems with locking and potential rollback failures. Instead, we have to carefully manage the deletion process, batching it to prevent performance issues. I think that we should make it such that it is idempotent and crash-safe.

The next consideration is the interaction of `AccountTenanted` and how this might interact with `Current.account`. It is important that the `incinerate` method operates independent of the `Current.account` and that all callbacks called within `account.incinerate` work correctly, even when a job is re-enqueued.

Now, what about the scope of the problem? The incineration process needs to touch every associated record: all tables, blobs, search indexes, callbacks, side effects, etc. Each entity needs to be handled carefully in a safe manner to prevent failures. This means iterating over everything, one-by-one.

We want to make sure an account can only be incinerated when it is cancellable. The method should lock and recheck the `cancellation` status *before* initiating any deletion, especially considering how `reactivate` can destroy `cancellation`. This prevents race conditions and ensures data consistency.

With all of this analysis, I'm confident we have a clear, safe, and efficient way to implement `Account::IncinerateDueJob`.

**Testing `in_batches` with Real Data and Transactional Rollbacks**

Okay, stop! Before we go any further, I need to get a handle on this `in_batches` behavior with some *real* data. I've realized the empty test database was throwing me a curveball, specifically that `Account.first` came back with zero cards – something I need to keep in mind, and that the fixtures aren't being loaded by `bin/rails runner` but are by `bin/rails test`. Right, so I need to make sure this is actually working as expected. Let's create some real records.

Specifically, I want to confirm `in_batches` *and* the `Search::Record::SQLite::Fts.where(rowid: ...).delete_all` interaction, with multiple records, and where the number of records is larger than the batch size (which is the whole point, right?). And, critically, let's wrap this in a rolled-back transaction. That's the only way to be sure we're not polluting the test environment with potentially unwanted side effects. I need to ensure this works as expected without altering the database itself.

arguments.command:
RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails runner '
ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
  account = Account.create!(name: "Batch Test")
  user = account.users.create!(name: "User", role: :owner)
  board = account.boards.create!(name: "Board", creator: user)
  5.times do |i|
    card = board.cards.create!(title: "Card #{i}", creator: user, status: :published)
    Search::Record.for(account.id).create!(
      account_id: account.id,
      searchable_type: "Card",
      searchable_id: card.id,
      card_id: card.id,
      board_id: board.id,
      title: card.title,
      content: "content #{i}",
      created_at: card.created_at
    )
  end

  batches = 0
  deleted = 0
  Card.where(account_id: account.id).in_batches(of: 2) do |batch|
    batches += 1
    deleted += batch.delete_all
  end
  puts "Card in_batches(of: 2): batches=#{batches} deleted=#{deleted} remaining=#{Card.where(account_id: account.id).count}"

  # Test Search::Record + Fts deletion
  sr_class = Search::Record.for(account.id)
  fts_before = Search::Record::SQLite::Fts.count
  sr_before = sr_class.where(account_id: account.id).count
  sr_class.where(account_id: account.id).in_batches(of: 2) do |batch|
    ids = batch.pluck(:id)
    Search::Record::SQLite::Fts.where(rowid: ids).delete_all
    batch.delete_all
  end
  puts "Search::Record before=#{sr_before} after=#{sr_class.where(account_id: account.id).count}; FTS before=#{fts_before} after=#{Search::Record::SQLite::Fts.count}"

  raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
end
'

Okay, wow! That output was impressive – every join table decremented by exactly one for the target account, and nothing else touched. Zero deprecation warnings, no UUID encoding bugs, bounded batch sizes, and it's working flawlessly on both SQLite and MySQL/Trilogy. But, as an expert, I know better than to get complacent. Let's dig deeper and think like a detective. Let's look for *every* subtle edge case!

Alright, first up, ActiveStorage. We need to meticulously trace every possible scenario and trace the impacts on storage:

1.  **Direct Attachments + Variants:** `Card#image`, `User#avatar` (including the `:thumb` variant with its immediate processing),
2.  **ActionText with Embeds:** `Card#description`, `Comment#body`, `Board#public_description` – all that rich text with embedded files adds a layer of complexity.
3.  **Exports and Imports:** `Account::Export#file`, `User::DataExport#file`, `Account::Import#file`—these need special consideration too.
4.  **Orphaned Blobs:** Think about blobs that are uploaded but never actually attached to any record!
5.  **Reused Blobs:** Copy-pasted ActionText embeds pointing to the same blob within the *same* account.
6.  **Cross-Account Shared Blobs:** What if `Storage::TEMPLATE_ACCOUNT_ID` were enabled? An attachment in Account B points to a blob owned by Template Account A.

    *   **Account B Incineration:** We delete Account B's `ActiveStorage::Attachment`s. We only purge blobs with `account_id: B`. So Template Account A's blob should NOT be touched.
    *   **Template Account A Incineration:** We delete Account A's `ActiveStorage::Attachment`s. If a blob owned by A is still linked to B, and we attempt `blob.purge`, `ActiveRecord::InvalidForeignKey` will be raised when `attachments.exists?` returns true. The `blob.purge` method should handle this gracefully and not break B's attachment.

7.  **Physical Files:** Make sure the corresponding files on disk or S3 are also deleted when the blob is purged! We have to call both `service.delete(key)` and `service.delete_prefixed("variants/#{key}/") if image?`.

8.  **Variant Edge Case:** A `User` in Account A uploads an avatar. Let's trace how the relationships are established in all the tables, so we can ensure the incinerator handles this case correctly, even with `Current.account` set correctly. Original blob `B1` is created with `account_id = A`. `User#avatar` attachment is created with `account_id = A`, `blob_id = B1.id`. Then, the `:thumb` variant runs (`process: :immediately`)!

    *   `ActiveStorage::VariantRecord` `V1` is created with `blob_id = B1.id`, `account_id = A`.
    *   Variant image blob `B2` is created with `account_id = A`.
    *   Variant image attachment `A2` is created with `record = V1`, `blob_id = B2.id`, `account_id = A`.

    We need to consider scenarios where a variant is processed later (background job, controller). We also need to check if `ActiveStorage::Blob#purge` fails if the file is missing from disk!

So, let's run a test in `bin/rails runner` and see!

user = account.users.create!(name: "User", role: :owner)
Current.set(account: account, user: user) do
  user.avatar.attach(io: File.open("test/fixtures/files/moon.jpg"), filename: "moon.jpg", content_type: "image/jpeg")
  # Force variant processing
  user.avatar.variant(:thumb).processed

  missing_blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create!(
    account: account,
    key: "nonexistent-key-#{SecureRandom.hex}",
    filename: "missing.txt",
    byte_size: 10,
    checksum: "abc",
    service_name: ActiveStorage::Blob.service.name
  )

  blobs = ActiveStorage::Blob.where(account_id: account.id).to_a
  keys = blobs.map(&:key)
  puts "BEFORE: attachments=#{ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(account_id: account.id).count} variants=#{ActiveStorage::VariantRecord.where(account_id: account.id).count} blobs=#{blobs.size}"
  puts "  files exist before: #{keys.map { |k| [k, ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(k)] }.inspect}"

  ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(account_id: account.id).in_batches(&:delete_all)
  ActiveStorage::VariantRecord.where(account_id: account.id).in_batches(&:delete_all)
  ActiveStorage::Blob.where(account_id: account.id).find_each(&:purge)

  puts "AFTER: attachments=#{ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(account_id: account.id).count} variants=#{ActiveStorage::VariantRecord.where(account_id: account.id).count} blobs=#{ActiveStorage::Blob.where(account_id: account.id).count}"
  puts "  files exist after: #{keys.map { |k| [k, ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(k)] }.inspect}"
end

User::Settings.where(account_id: account.id).delete_all

**Analyzing Recurring Job Scheduling in Fizzy**

Okay, so Solid Queue's Solid Queue tables aren't relevant for this test since we're using the `:test` queue adapter in the test SQLite database. That's fine; we can bypass that concern and directly verify Fugit schedule parsing, as Solid Queue leverages Fugit under the hood. The direct approach is often cleaner anyway! Let's get to the core of the matter: verifying how `config/recurring.yml` parses with `Fugit.parse`.

I'm looking at `config/recurring.yml`. I see the recurring jobs defined and I'm focusing on the schedules. Specifically, these entries catch my eye:

*   `auto_postpone_all_due`: `every hour at minute 50`
*   `delete_unused_tags`: `every day at 04:02`
*   `incinerate_due_accounts`: `every day at 04:30` (or `every hour at minute 30`)

The key distinction is the "every hour" versus "every day" schedules. Let's compare a few entries to understand the possible patterns:

*   Under *Application cleanup* `auto_postpone_all_due` schedule is every hour at minute 50.
*   Under *Application cleanup* `delete_unused_tags` uses a Class and is scheduled every day at 04:02.
*   Under *Operations cleanup and backups* `clear_solid_queue_finished_jobs` runs every hour at minute 12.

Now, focusing on the `incinerate_due_accounts` job, the choice between "every hour at minute 30" and "every day at 04:30" warrants careful consideration.

Let's break down the advantages of `every hour at minute 30`:

1.  **No Schedule Collisions**: It avoids collisions with jobs scheduled for minutes 12, 20, 25, or 50. That's a solid check.
2.  **Timely Incineration**: Accounts canceled more than 30 days ago are incinerated within an hour of the threshold instead of waiting up to 24 hours. The granularity is improved.
3.  **Resilience to Interruptions**: If a worker gets interrupted or there's a surge in cancellations, the job resumes within an hour, reducing potential delays.
4.  **Efficiency when Empty**: When no accounts are due, it's a lightweight database query, avoiding unnecessary overhead.

And, of course, the `development` environment automatically inherits this configuration due to the `*production` reference. This is a sound structure.

**Deep Dive into Account Incineration**

Okay, here's the deal. I need to make *absolutely* sure that `account.destroy!` runs *as the very last step*. If it doesn't, we're asking for trouble, big time. I'm thinking, what if we've already loaded a bunch of associations into memory *before* calling `incinerate`? You know, like in a test where we have `account.users`, `account.boards`, and `account.cards` cached? If we delete rows using `User.where(account_id: id).in_batches(&:delete_all)` and then just call `account.destroy!` *without* a `reload`, we're going to iterate over stale, cached objects. This is bad. *Very* bad, because that means we'd be calling `.destroy` on those cached objects, potentially triggering a cascade of unintended callbacks and side effects, and generally making a huge mess.

On the other hand, if we call `reload.destroy!`, that changes everything! *Reload* clears the cached associations. So, the database is queried, and it's empty, except for `cancellation` and the `account`. Calling `destroy!` then only destroys these two, and nothing else! We avoid those stale objects completely. Plus, it's super efficient – a few empty `SELECT` queries are negligible. And, this also acts as a safety net if we add a new `dependent: :destroy` association to `Account` in the future!

So, the plan:
1.  **Bulk Data Deletion**: We're going to execute the bulk data deletions first:
    *   `purge_active_storage` (attachments, variants, blobs)
    *   `delete_search_records`
    *   `delete_storage_totals`
    *   `delete_filters`
    *   `delete_account_scoped_records` (in batches)
2.  **Atomic Destruction with Reload**: This is where it gets interesting – a  `reload.destroy!`:
    *   Reload clears cached associations.
    *   Destroys `account.cancellation` and `account` inside a transaction.
    *   This also takes care of *any* `dependent: :destroy` associations – good for engines and extensions!
    *   Marks the account as `destroyed? == true` and freezes it.
    *   No background jobs, no Turbo broadcasts.

Now, a quick check on `Account::StorageLimited` (SaaS): I need to add `dependent: :destroy` to `has_one :storage_exception`. It's safe, and improves cleanup!

And another check with `Storage::Entry.record`: It's crucial because we *don't* want to record storage for deleted accounts. Earlier the code would crash due to passing the account object rather than its id. Now, `account.destroyed?` correctly identifies that this model is no longer available. Checking the tests confirms this behavior.

So, in summary: `reload.destroy!` is the key to safe and efficient account incineration. It prevents stale object iteration, ensures atomic destruction, and provides a safety net for future associations.

**Deep Dive into Account Incineration Implementation**

Okay, let's break this down meticulously. First, the core concept: `config.x.multi_tenant.enabled = true` in test is irrelevant here. If an `Account::Cancellation` exists beyond 30 days, we *incinerate* it regardless of the `multi_tenant` setting. No conditional check is needed. That's clear.

Now, the critical question: what happens if multiple accounts are due for incineration, and one throws an error in `Account::IncinerateDueJob`? Time for a rigorous thought experiment.

The natural inclination, based on prior patterns with jobs like `DeleteUnusedTagsJob`, `Export.cleanup`, `Account::Import.cleanup`, and so on, is to *not* rescue exceptions. Letting errors bubble up immediately provides a clear backtrace during development and testing. Solid Queue handles retries or surfaces these issues in monitoring tools like Mission Control and Sentry. That is what we are seeing here.

Rescuing `StandardError` would be tempting because of `SearchReindexJob` that rescues `StandardError`. However, that is the *exception* that proves the rule. The only job of that type is `SearchReindexJob`, which is an ad-hoc, manual repair script. In tests, it can mask a real problem. All recurring jobs, and cleanup tasks, intentionally let errors surface for immediate attention. That's the correct approach.

Next, logging? Do we even *need* logging for this particular job? Following the existing cleanup jobs (`DeleteUnusedTagsJob`, `Export.cleanup`, `Account::Import.cleanup`, `Webhook::Delivery.cleanup`, `MagicLink.cleanup`), there is no logging. We stick with the existing pattern. This keeps things clean, idiomatic, and consistent across the Fizzy project. No logging.

Now, a very subtle but important point. Let's trace how this behaves within the framework of ActiveJob::TestCase:
`Account::IncinerateDueJob.perform_now` works as expected, and that's simple. Let's see what happens if the enqueued job is used by `perform_later`.

Let's say in a test scenario, `Current.account` is set, and we cancel the account and then advance time. We call `Account::IncinerateDueJob.perform_later`. `AccountTenanted#initialize` captures the `Current.account`. `AccountTenanted#serialize` writes this account's Global ID (GID).  When `perform_enqueued_jobs` is called, `AccountTenanted#resolve_account!` locates the account. The job will then execute as expected.

BUT what happens if, *before* `perform_enqueued_jobs` is called, the account is deleted? `resolve_account!` would raise `ActiveJob::DeserializationError`. It appears our recurring job's setup is incorrect! This job operates across *all* accounts in the database, not a single tenant. `Notification::Bundle::DeliverAllJob` sets `discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError` is a perfect model for this. This instructs Solid Queue to discard the job upon that error condition. That fixes it!

If `Account::IncinerateDueJob` inherits from `ApplicationJob`, it will inherit the default `AccountTenanted` setup. In a production context, `Current.account` will be `nil`. But in tests, an account might be set. *Within* `Account::Incineration#run`, we use `Current.without_account` which *ensures* `Current.account` doesn't affect the operation of incinerating other accounts! That's the key. This is the idiomatic way.

The job should *not* attempt to set `self.account = nil`, to fight the inherited `AccountTenanted` behavior. The established pattern from `DeleteUnusedTagsJob`, `SearchReindexJob`, and `Notification::Bundle::DeliverAllJob` means we simply inherit from `ApplicationJob` and rely on `Current.without_account`. Perfect.

Lastly, the `config/recurring.yml` entry needs scrutiny:
*   The key is `incinerate_due_accounts`, which is consistent.
*   The `class` is explicitly set to `Account::IncinerateDueJob`. Check.
*   The schedule is `every hour at minute 30` which looks good.
*   Finally, the `queue` is already set as `:backend` in the job itself, so it will respect the jobs configuration.

I think we've covered all the bases!
